key_insight: Introducing checklist-style rewards provides verifiable intermediate signals that make reinforcement learning effective for multi-turn, multi-step agentic tool use without requiring fully executable tool environments.
problem_solved: Enables RL for open-ended, multi-turn tool-using agents where final rewards are sparse or unverifiable and constructing full tool environments is costly.
method: Design checklist rewards that decompose tasks into verifiable intermediate subgoals and provide dense, structured feedback during multi-turn interactions.
Train agents with RL using these checklist rewards to guide multi-step tool invocations and dialogue policies across turns.
Evaluate agentic tool use without exhaustive executable environments by validating subgoal completion and chain-of-actions instead of relying solely on terminal success signals.
impact: Makes RL practical for complex conversational agents that must coordinate multiple tools and steps, reducing environment engineering overhead and improving learning stability and interpretability.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: user query → checklist of subgoals → agent planning & tool calls → checklist verification → RL update loop
Multi-turn timeline: annotated dialogue turns showing subgoal checks and tool invocations
Bar chart: performance comparison (success rate, sample efficiency) between checklist-reward RL and standard sparse-reward baselines
Icon set: checklist, toolbox (external tools), dialogue bubbles, and reward signal to convey core concepts at a glance
paper_title: CM2: Reinforcement Learning with Checklist Rewards for Multi-Turn and Multi-Step Agentic Tool Use
paper_authors: Zhen Zhang, Kaiqiang Song, Xun Wang, Yebowen Hu, Weixiang Yan
